item.title: Server approval
item.description:
The helper runs as root (SYSTEM on Windows) and a server it enrolls with chooses the routes and the peer of the machine’s tunnel: a hostile server is every packet of the machine, sent there. Since client v0.11.0 the helper takes a server from the app only if one of these holds:

  1. the administrator’s configuration names it (servers in helper.json, now optional: the pre-approval);
  2. it was approved before, and still says what it said then;
  3. it is approved now, with the consent of the operating system, obtained by the helper itself.

An app flag, a field of the request, or a claim of any kind is never consent.

What is asked of the system

Platform Consent
macOS Authorization Services right com.claimward.helper.approve-server, rule authenticate-admin-nonshared: an administrator’s name and password, every time. The app obtains the authorization (macauth.Obtain) and sends its 32-byte external form; the helper has the system verify it and destroys it, so one token buys one approval. A forged token names nothing in the system and is refused
Linux polkit action com.claimward.helper.approve-server (auth_admin), asked of the system bus for the process behind the socket: its pid from SO_PEERCRED and its start time from /proc/<pid>/stat, which defeats pid reuse. The policy file ships in packaging/polkit/ and goes in /usr/share/polkit-1/actions/
Windows a second socket, C:\ProgramData\Claimward\approve.sock, whose ACL names SYSTEM and Administrators only: a standard user cannot connect without UAC elevation. Only a request that came in on it counts

With no authorizer configured the helper refuses every approval: it fails closed. A request that is refused, or that the system cannot answer, changes nothing.

What is remembered

The helper keeps the approved servers in a file only root can write:

Platform File
macOS /var/db/claimward/approved-servers.json
Linux /var/lib/claimward/approved-servers.json
Windows C:\ProgramData\Claimward\approved-servers.json

Each entry is the server’s canonical URL and the SHA-256 of its discovery identity: its name and its identity providers (id, kind, issuer, client ids). A server that changes one of those is not the one that was approved: the helper refuses it (server_identity_changed) until it is approved again. Whether the server is exclusive, its logo and the providers’ display names are not part of the identity, and neither is its TLS certificate, which is renewed every few weeks (the connection is verified against the web PKI at each use).

The file is read afresh at every use, so deleting it, or removing a line, revokes at once; the revoke action does the same for one server. An administrator’s servers list is never edited by the helper.

Errors the app sees

Code Meaning
server_not_approved the server is neither pre-approved nor approved: ask the person to approve it
server_identity_changed it was approved, and no longer says the same: approve it again
approval_denied the system’s consent was not given

Limits, stated

  • On macOS the text of the prompt is supplied by the app that asks, so a hostile process in the socket’s group can make the system ask an administrator to approve its own server, and a distracted administrator can say yes. The credential is an administrator’s, never cached, and good for one approval.
  • On Windows, an elevated process can approve anything, as an administrator can edit the file anyway.
  • Linux has no cache either: auth_admin asks every time.
